newsitem.title: USA: Sierra Pacific to realign Alturas power line plan.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Pacific to realign Alturas power line plan.

text.p: Sierra Pacific Power Co said Wednesday it will seek approval from the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to move a small portion of a planned transmission line following the U.S. Forest Service's decision not to allow the project.

Modoc Forest Supervisor Diane Henderson-Bramlette notified the company Wednesday it cannot buld a 2.8 mile section of a 345 kilovolt tranmission line in a portion of the forest west of Alturas, Calif.
In a letter to Sierra Pacific, she said there are other "environmentally acceptable routes that would accomplish your company's purpose..."

"We're disappointed with the decision, but we have a fully studied alternate route off the Modoc Forest that was identified during the environmental review process," said Alturas Project Manager John Owens.
That route would change the first five miles of the transmission line near Alturas and require construction of a substation on privately owned land.
The Forest Service decision does not change the route in Nevada or the other 131 miles of the route already approved in California, the company said.
Pending state approvals, Sierra Pacific said it hopes to start construction of the power line in the fall of 1997 and have it completed by late 1998.
The Alturas Intertie project is aimed at providing the northern Nevada-northern California area with an additional 300 megawatts of electricity from the Pacific Northwest.
